title: Astrid and the Contact
premise: Mara Almeida, a financial-crimes investigator who launders the reputations of cases too sensitive to prosecute, discovers the safe house protecting his star witness has been listed online — interior photos, floor plans, everything. The leak traces back inside his own agency, and the witness, a quiet accountant named Astrid, is the only person who can decode the ledger behind a staged 'accident' timed to the Geneva summit. As Mara burns his career to keep Astrid alive, he learns the attack's architect is the mentor who taught him that clean money is a kindness. In the end, Mara chooses justice outside the law: he lets the summit proceed under a manufactured paper trail that exposes the conspirators publicly, then disappears with Astrid into a found family of exiles who owe him everything.
about_author: August Pemberton is a former compliance officer who spent eleven years watching money move through places it should never have reached before leaving to write about the people caught in its current. He lives off-grid on the Baltic coast and refuses interviews.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Scrolling property sites at 2 a.m., he finds the safe house for sale — twelve photos of Astrid's kitchen, her coat on the hook. Panic masquerading as procedure: he calls the duty line and gets voicemail. Emotional beat: the cold realization that someone wanted this seen.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, flashback-woven. We learn his job: making prosecutions disappear into accounting errors, 'cleaning' cases no one wants attributed. His mentor Ivo Kessler taught him that mercy is paperwork. Beat: Mara's pride curdling as he realizes he's part of the machine he now fears.

chapters.title: Astrid
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She notices the realtor's drone pass twice in one afternoon and starts packing without being told. Her competence and calm contrast with Mara's arrival, breathless and armed. Beat: two strangers negotiating trust in a hallway of packed boxes.

chapters.title: Twelve Photos
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Forensic review of the listing metadata points to an agency-issued camera and a login from inside the Directorate. He can't report it without confirming Astrid's location. Beat: isolation — the protector realizing the institution itself is the threat.

chapters.title: The Ledger She Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She explains what she stole: a shadow ledger mapping shell payments to a logistics firm contracted for summit security. She doesn't know what the payments bought; she only knows they were hidden twice. Beat: dawning scale — this isn't embezzlement, it's infrastructure.

chapters.title: Roads Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Every extraction route he requests gets quietly denied or delayed. He goes off-book, borrowing a car from a retired colleague, Tomas, who asks no questions but hands him a burner phone. Beat: first seed of found family — help given freely, outside channels.

chapters.title: Kessler
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A tense dinner with his mentor, who warns him gently that some listings are messages, not mistakes. Kessler offers to make the problem disappear — Mara's problem being, ambiguously, the house or Astrid. Beat: charm with teeth; the reader sees the trap before Mara does.

chapters.title: Safe House Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A farmhouse outside Basel, paid in cash by Tomas's cousin Lena, a former field medic. Domestic scenes: Astrid teaching Lena's daughter card tricks, Mara unable to sleep. Beat: fragile warmth the reader knows is borrowed time.

chapters.title: The Accident File
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cross-referencing the ledger with summit logistics, he finds a prior 'accident' — a gas explosion in Rotterdam that killed an auditor. Same contractor, same insurance structure. Beat: horror of pattern recognition; the attack will look like negligence, not malice.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Her old credentials are used to access a system she never touched — someone is building a case against her. She understands she's being pre-positioned as the fall scapegoat. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance; she stops running and starts working.

chapters.title: What the Money Bought
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The ledger decodes fully: payments for industrial refrigerant diverted to a tunnel beneath the summit's hotel annex — enough to stage a catastrophic 'gas failure.' Timeline: nine days. Beat: ticking clock engaged; Mara must choose between reporting up (compromised) or acting alone.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me
chapters.summary: Extended flashback chapter, Mara's POV. How Kessler recruited him, saved him after a scandal, taught him that unattributed justice was the only honest kind left. Beat: tragic intimacy — the reader now loves and fears Kessler equally.

chapters.title: Lena's Rules
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She lays down house rules: no names, no phones inside, everyone cooks. Under her discipline the fugitives become a household. Beat: found family crystallizing — the safest place in the book is also the most exposed.

chapters.title: Inside Job
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. He identifies the leaker: Deputy Director Halloran, whose signature appears on both the Rotterdam cover-up and the listing approval. Confronting him means burning every protection Mara has. Beat: point of no return declared out loud.

chapters.title: The Trap at the Annex
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She insists on visiting the annex's utility records in person, disguised as an insurance surveyor. She photographs the refrigerant transfer logs but trips a sensor. Beat: competence under terror; she escapes by minutes, changed by what she's capable of.

chapters.title: Betrayal Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Kessler reveals he knew all along — and offers Mara a place beside him, arguing the attack will kill fewer people than the war its exposure would start. The utilitarian seduction, delivered with genuine love. Beat: the book's moral crux; Mara almost says yes.

chapters.title: No Attribution
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, night scene. He refuses: justice that hides isn't justice, it's management. He walks out knowing Kessler will now hunt them both. Calls Tomas, Lena, and two other ghosts from his past. Beat: resolve; the loner finally asking for help.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating POVs. The improvised team plans exposure, not rescue: mirror the ledger into press inboxes, regulators, and three governments simultaneously, timed to the summit's opening session. Beat: caper energy rising over dread; each member contributes their one true skill.

chapters.title: Kessler's Move
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Kessler's people find the farmhouse; Lena's early-warning drills save them. In the escape, Tomas takes a bullet shielding Astrid and survives, barely. Beat: cost made real; the family bleeds but holds.

chapters.title: The Summit Opens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. He infiltrates the annex's control room to physically block the refrigerant release while the data dump fires worldwide. Kessler arrives personally. Beat: climax — two men who love the same idea of order, holding opposite triggers.

chapters.title: Accidents, Prevented
chapters.summary: Climax resolution, Mara's POV. Mara doesn't fight Kessler; he shows him the live feed of the exposé landing — the attack is now worthless, its architects named. Kessler, undone by transparency rather than force, surrenders to the arriving police with terrible dignity. Beat: catharsis through truth instead of violence.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Months later: hearings, resignations, Halloran indicted. Mara, officially resigned and unofficially erased, keeps the farmhouse with Astrid, Lena, and recovering Tomas. No plaque, no attribution — just a new listing never posted anywhere. Beat: quiet, earned peace; found family as the final safe house.
